routes.label: Prove a bound and attain it

question: The sum of seven integers is \(-1.\) What is the maximum number of the seven integers that can be larger than \(13?\)
solution:
An integer larger than \(13\) must be at least \(14\). If all seven integers were larger than \(13\), their sum would be at least
\[
7\times14=98,
\]
which cannot equal \(-1\). Thus at most six can be larger than \(13\).

To show that six are possible, choose six integers equal to \(14\) and the seventh equal to \(-85\). Repeated values are allowed, and
\[
6\times14+(-85)=84-85=-1.
\]
Exactly six of these integers exceed \(13\), so the maximum is \(6\), choice D.
